page: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64gb is a memory-optimized cloud server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an AMD EPYC processor running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a minimal 1 GB NVMe SSD, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded CPU capability alongside balanced multi-core execution. The processor achieves top-tier scores in stress-ng single-core execution, gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside strong Geekbench single-core and text processing metrics. Multithreaded synthetic performance sits in the middle tier, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 8045.0 and PassMark CPU reaching 18458.78. Memory throughput shows 72.42 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 41.4 GB/sec on writes, supporting 15.44 million Redis SET operations per second.

The primary operational tradeoff lies in the storage configuration. The instance supplies 1 GB of local NVMe storage, meaning persistent large-capacity storage must be provisioned externally. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high memory density per compute core, making it an efficient allocation for RAM-intensive tasks that do not require proportional multi-core compute overhead. Its instruction set features comprehensive vector extensions, including AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI.

Vultr vx1-m-8c-64gb fits workloads that require large in-memory working sets alongside dedicated compute stability. Appropriate deployment scenarios include Redis or Memcached caching tiers, in-memory databases, text-processing pipelines, intermediate ETL stages, and lightweight inference runtimes utilizing smaller language models.
